transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-04-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Hannah Park (Redwood SE); Raj Patel (LumenHealth Eng Manager); Sofia Martinez (LumenHealth ML Eng); Tom Blake (LumenHealth Product); Ibrahim Noor (LumenHealth Security)

Summary: quick review of the last week's pilot runs, SDK integration blockers, function/tool calling examples for extracting structured patient-summary JSON, handling streaming partials, and next steps for benchmarks and security docs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining.. we'll keep to 40 mins, quick status then deep dive into the SDK function call stuff, and structured output.
[00:22] Raj Patel: Yeah thanks Maya, we ran the three prompt sets you asked last week, saw variability in the structured fields. sometimes "medList" got flattened, sometimes missing dosage units.
[00:40] Sofia Martinez: and hi, quick note, streaming helped with perceived latency but we saw a couple of truncated JSON payloads in the middle of the stream which our parser choked on.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: ok good, so two topics: (1) model output variability — we have SDK helpers for schema enforcement and function/tool calling; (2) streaming partials — we recommend a framing/assembler on client side plus the SDK has a small validator.
[01:35] Tom Blake: can you remind us which SDK you sent? we pulled the python one, we also have a node backend.
[01:50] Maya Chen: yes sent python and node example links in the last email, link: https://redwood.dev/sdk-sample - but we'll attach the new snippet after this call that shows function calling + structured output type hints.
[02:20] Sofia Martinez: the issue is our consumer expects a strict schema {patient_id, medList:[{name,dose,unit}], allergies:[]}. When dose units are missing our validation fails and the pipeline stops.
[02:50] Hannah Park: we've seen that in other pilots; two approaches — 1) use explicit function/tool calls where the model returns typed arguments (Redwood function calling) and we map to typed objects; 2) use post-generation schema validation with fill-in prompts to repair missing fields.
[03:12] Ibrahim Noor: quick security question - when using function calls are we sending PII over the hosted API? what's the retention?
[03:30] Maya Chen: good Q - for the pilot you're on hosted EU region so data is processed in-region and retention defaults are minimal, we can enable no-retain/ephemeral mode for the POC. we'll follow up with the SOC2/ISO3 checklist.
[04:00] Raj Patel: sounds good. on the function calling, we tried to use it but the SDK returned an error 'bad_schema' sometimes; stack trace attached in the run-logs we uploaded.
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: can you paste the snippet? oftentimes that's because the model returned a top-level string rather than the JSON object expected. our SDK has a parser that attempts a best-effort parse, but we also added a validator layer to reject and re-prompt the model with a repair instruction.
[04:45] Sofia Martinez: here's the snippet from logs: (reads) "function_response: \"{\\\"medList\\\": [\\\"aspirin\\\", \\\"lisinopril\\\"]}\"" — so it's returning a list of strings not objects.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: mm-hmm, that looks like the model collapsed to a short form. We can show two fixes: a) stricter function schema with typed arrays of objects b) post-processing that maps string tokens to objects with a small lookup + confidence threshold.
[05:30] Maya Chen: also note quantization + model variant can change tokenization and therefore output patterns; for a POC we recommend a stable model family — we had the Redwood-Base-quant12 behave differently than Redwood-Standard-8.
[05:55] Raj Patel: ok, we used Redwood-Base-quant12 for cost reasons. Might switch to standard for the pilot if latency's still fine.
[06:20] Tom Blake: can you give us an idea of the latency delta? we have a 300ms SLO for patient-facing flows.
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: ballpark from the recent runs: standard-8 avg token latency ~45ms per token; quant12 optimized ~65ms per token but lower cost. For typical 30-token function payloads that means ~1.3s vs ~2s end-to-end — still within your 3s target but perceptible.
[07:05] Sofia Martinez: those numbers match roughly what we measured, though we saw heavy spikes during batching windows.
[07:25] Hannah Park: batching and prefix cache can spike tail latency if not tuned; SDK allows you to set batch window target and cache TTL for prefix responses. For this pilot we've set a small batch window to keep latency tight.
[07:50] Raj Patel: about streaming truncated JSON — any recommended patterns? we saw incomplete chunks like "{\"patient_id\": 123, \"medList\": [ {\"name\": \"aspi"" then end of stream.
[08:10] Liam O'Connor: yes implement an assembler that waits for the stream to close or a terminal token before JSON parse; the SDK emits 'chunk' events and 'end' event. Also the SDk exposes a 'safe_parse' helper that concats and retries parse with small back-off. We'll include that.
[08:40] Sofia Martinez: would prefer examples in Node — our backend service is Node.
[08:50] Maya Chen: noted, we'll push node examples.
[09:05] Tom Blake: any infra changes needed to use function calling? like extra endpoints?
[09:15] Hannah Park: no, it sits in the same API call; you pass a functions schema object in the request body. The SDK wraps it. For on-prem/private it's the same API surface with local endpoint.
[09:35] Ibrahim Noor: about encryption, KMS - can we hold keys? we need HSM support for pilot prod parity.
[09:45] Maya Chen: yes private and dedicated customers can bring their own KMS/HSM; for the hosted pilot we can integrate with customer-managed KMS in the EU region. I'll get the architecture note to you.
[10:05] Raj Patel: thanks. On errors — we saw intermittent 'rate-limited' 429s during a 10-min spike, is that expected in pilot?
[10:20] Liam O'Connor: for hosted free-tier maybe yes, but for pilot we can bump up quotas or recommend dedicated capacity. For now we can apply a temporary quota increase for your account.
[10:35] Sofia Martinez: if we do dedicated later, what's the minimum commit?
[10:40] Maya Chen: generally monthly reserved capacity starts at a small pool, but I'll have AE follow up with pricing.
[10:50] Tom Blake: re: structured output: could you walk through the function schema we should be using for patient-summary?
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: sure — recommended schema (high-level): name: patient_summary, params: { patient_id: string, medList: array of objects {name:string,dose:string,unit:string,confidence:float}, allergies: array of strings, notes: string }. We'll attach the exact JSON schema in the SDK sample. Also include an enum for unit types to avoid freeform units.
[11:45] Raj Patel: we have a canonical medical unit mapping, can we provide that as a enums list?
[11:55] Hannah Park: yes pass that as part of the function schema; model will pick from the enum ideally. If not, post-validate and map synonyms.
[12:15] Sofia Martinez: any recommendations for partial repair prompts? when items are missing.
[12:30] Liam O'Connor: we do a 2-step: initial response -> validate -> if missing fields invoke a repair function call with the violations and ask the model to fill. SDK automates that loop in example code.
[12:55] Tom Blake: on streaming and UI — can we stream partial structured data to the UI (e.g., progressively render meds)?
[13:10] Maya Chen: yes, but you must ensure each partial chunk is either a full element or annotated with indices. The SDK's streaming mode emits structured events if you pass streamSchema: true. We'll show example.
[13:40] Raj Patel: about test harness — we uploaded 3 prompt scenarios; which ones should we prioritize?
[13:50] Liam O'Connor: prioritize: 1) highly structured with full fields (sanity), 2) messy shorthand notes (real-world), 3) adversarial missing units. We'll run the same under two models and collect token/latency/cost.
[14:10] Sofia Martinez: sounds good. we'll run those.
[14:20] Maya Chen: quick recap of logs we need: attach run traces, raw model outputs (incl stream chunks), and API request ids. That lets us correlate on our side.
[14:40] Raj Patel: done. we uploaded run-logs.zip to the shared folder.
[14:50] Ibrahim Noor: last security point - audit logs and RBAC - can we see per-token ingestion logs? we need to prove PII access control.
[15:05] Hannah Park: Redwood Console supports per-route tracing and token-level breakdowns; for hosted we can provide audit export. We'll include a sample export. For private/dedicated you get more granular controls.
[15:25] Tom Blake: ok, sounds like action items are clear. any blockers to running the additional benchmarks?
[15:35] Sofia Martinez: just need the node SDK snippet for streaming and the safe_parse helper; otherwise we'll run next week.
[15:45] Liam O'Connor: we'll send that today.
[15:50] Maya Chen: good. final Q from my side — timeline for pilot switch to EU-hosted no-retain? you wanted by mid-April?
[16:00] Raj Patel: yes, we aim to run production-sim tests by 2025-04-20 so need data residency confirmed by 2025-04-12.
[16:10] Maya Chen: noted, I'll follow-up with security pack and confirm.
[16:25] Tom Blake: great, thanks everyone.
[16:30] Maya Chen: thanks — we'll send notes and updated snippets; next sync same time next week.

End of transcript.

References/Artifacts:
- run-logs.zip (uploaded to shared drive)
- SDK sample links: https://redwood.dev/sdk-sample (will attach node streaming + safe_parse)
- Security docs link (to be shared): https://redwood.dev/security/soc2
